prerequisites: Mathematics and Physics knowledge from basic courses offered in the first two years.

learning_outcomes.text: understand the theoretical aspects of Fluid Mechanics and their properties
mathematically formulate and apply the conservation principles of fluid mechanics
quantitatively solve applied problems related to flows in pressure pipes

syllabus_topics: Introductory concepts (4 hours): Characterization of a fluid as a continuous system. No-slip condition. Physical properties of fluids (density, specific weight, compressibility). Viscosity: Newtonian, non-Newtonian, perfect fluids. Vapor pressure, surface tension and capillarity.

Fluid Statics (12 hours): Concept of pressure. Fundamental equations of the pressure field for compressible and incompressible fluids. Hydrostatic pressure distribution. Graphical representation of pressures. Pressure measurement (barometers and piezometers, manometers). Hydrostatic forces on flat and curved surfaces. Hydrostatic paradox (Pascal's barrel). Buoyancy. Pressure measurement.

Introduction to Fluid Dynamics. Bernoulli's Theorem (8 hours): Derivation of Bernoulli's theorem. Energetic interpretation. Static pressure, dynamic pressure, total pressure and stagnation point. Applications of Bernoulli's theorem: i) confined fluids, ii) Siphon and cavitation, iii) Free jets, iv) flow meters. Total head line and piezometric line. Efflux law.

Fluid Kinematics (5 hours): The velocity field: Eulerian and Lagrangian approach. Streamlines, flow tubes and trajectories. The acceleration field: the total derivative. Control volume and system representation. Reynolds Transport Theorem. Choice of control volume.

Global Equations of Hydrodynamics (8 hours): The continuity equation - principle of mass conservation - derivation and applications. Newton's second law - Momentum theorem: derivation and applications. First principle of thermodynamics - energy equation: derivation and applications.

Differential Equations of Hydrodynamics (4 hours): Mass conservation. The momentum equation: stress tensor, Cauchy's equations. Real viscous fluids: stress-strain relations, Navier-Stokes equations, laminar flow between two flat plates and Couette flow.

Dimensional Analysis, Similarity and Models (4 hours): Non-dimensionalization of equations. Buckingham's theorem. Significant dimensionless groups in fluid mechanics: Reynolds number, Froude number. Models and similarities.

Viscous Fluid Flows in Pressure (5 hours): General characteristics of pipe flows: laminar and turbulent flow, entrance region and fully developed flow region. Velocity distribution in laminar flow. Distributed losses in laminar flow: Darcy-Weisbach equation. Turbulent flow: wall law, logarithmic law, power law of velocity distribution in turbulent flow. Distributed losses in turbulent flow: Colebrook formula and Moody diagram. Localized losses.
assessment_rules: The assessment is divided into two parts: a written exam and an oral exam. The written exam evaluates competencies through exercise solving. The oral exam verifies the achievement of theoretical and applied learning objectives. The oral exam can only be taken after passing the written exam and must occur within the same examination session. The final grade is a weighted average of the scores from both parts.
